impact: Korea and Taiwan are on the list, raising costs and retaliation risk across the chip supply chain that feeds MU, DRAM and SNXX and weighing on SKM's home market; the delay before taking effect leaves room for deals.
summary: USTR Jamieson Greer on November 25 proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners after an eight-month probe into excess industrial capacity: China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the EU, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. China faces a 20% rate stacked on the 25% 2018 tariffs, which could rise to 40% without a favorable deal, with an exemption proposed for about $30 billion of Chinese goods; the other new tariffs will not stack on duties finalized in July. Greer does not expect them to take effect for at least a couple of months, pending public comment and a hearing. China called the overcapacity rationale a false proposition.
title: US proposes Section 301 tariffs on 14 partners; China faces extra 20%
